value.hook: Read before changing role-send claiming, boot recovery or cold-drain audits.
value.title: Role queue claims and recovery admission

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Role-send review lesson from PR #129, head 314da13a19d8d233e8c7b6d48d3de0991635b47e.

Claim queued work atomically against the current live project/role/instance assignment. A release before claim must prevent stale hooks from consuming later requests. Authorization linearizes at claim; it is not retroactive revocation of already-admitted work.

Recovery evidence must identify the holder/recipient, message ID and local origin. Authenticated foreign-origin rows are not local delivery evidence. The reviewed implementation relies on the existing local delivery-ID contract rather than separately comparing body/project/role or every job state.

A queued delivery job or held FYI records admission, not model completion. A transactional recovery pass is not universal exactly-once proof; this version logs recovery failure and continues startup. Distinguish those limits from the correctness of its atomic row updates.

Cold-drain overrides require the stored request identity and a mandatory audit before dispatch. Audit failure must not wake the holder. This assignment/queue policy is separate from future requester-reply wake enforcement.

CI run 42174918545 tested the exact source tree with 1968 passing JUnit cases. Its restart regression invokes boot over seeded claims, not live process killing. Foreign-origin/corrupt-job recovery and audit-bus failure were source-assessed, not dedicated fault-injection runs. Never upgrade those evidence grades in a later handoff.
